sources.title: Protecting Personal Information: A Guide for Business
sources.appliedPrinciple: Collect only what is needed, keep it only as long as necessary, protect it and dispose of it under a written retention approach.

sources.title: Collecting, Using, or Sharing Consumer Health Information? Look to HIPAA, the FTC Act, and the Health Breach Notification Rule
sources.appliedPrinciple: Take a broad view of sensitive health-related information, make data flows and retention truthful, and require meaningful consent rather than deceptive or coercive interfaces.

sources.title: Privacy Principles
sources.appliedPrinciple: Use the stable W3C privacy principles as a technical design reference for purpose limitation, data minimization and user control.

sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: Privacy Framework
sources.appliedPrinciple: Treat privacy as an ongoing risk-management system with clear governance, control, communication and protection outcomes.

implementationDecision: Pre56 uses an explicit opt-in plus a separate server enablement flag, allowlisted dimensions, aggregate-only storage, 30-day retention, minimum-denominator reporting and no third-party analytics. This is a product design control, not a claim of blanket legal compliance.
